# Vendored: node-stratum-pool

- Upstream: https://github.com/zone117x/node-stratum-pool
- Commit: `d1e71da` (2024-06-03)
- Authors: Matthew Little, with contributions from vekexasia and TheSeven (per the upstream `package.json`)
- License: GPL-2.0, see [LICENSE](./LICENSE). This repository is distributed under the same license.

## Local modifications

Apart from `require` lines, a few small robustness and security fixes differ from upstream.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/algoProperties.js` | `multi-hashing` is replaced by [`lib/multiHashing.js`](../../lib/multiHashing.js), which provides `scrypt` through `crypto.scryptSync`. The native module does not compile on current Node.js. Other algorithms in that file fail if selected; the pool configuration only permits `scrypt`. |
| `lib/algoProperties.js`, `lib/blockTemplate.js`, `lib/jobManager.js`, `lib/util.js` | `bignum` is replaced by [`lib/bignum.js`](../../lib/bignum.js), a `BigInt` implementation of the subset the pool uses. The npm `bignum` package has an unpatched high-severity advisory (GHSA-6429-3g3w-6mw5, `powm`, which the pool never calls) and needs a native build. |
| `lib/util.js` | `base58-native` (which depends on `bignum`) is replaced by [`lib/base58.js`](../../lib/base58.js). Unlike the original it throws on characters outside the alphabet. |
| `lib/stratum.js` | `handleMessage` defaults a missing or non-array `params` to `[]`, and `handleSubmit` replies with error 20 unless all five submit params are strings. Previously a message such as `{"method":"mining.submit"}` from an authorized worker threw in `processShare` and crashed the pool. Submissions are attributed to the authorized worker name instead of the name sent in the submit params. The job rebroadcast timer re-arms itself; previously a template refresh that failed during a daemon outage stopped rebroadcasts until the next new block. | `mining.configure` declines each requested extension; `mining.extranonce.subscribe`, `mining.suggest_difficulty`, `mining.suggest_target`, `mining.get_transactions` and unknown methods with a request id receive an error reply (`get_transactions` previously answered with `id: null`). Adds `messageRateLimit`/`messageRateWindow` (fixed-window count of received lines per connection, on a monotonic clock) and `maxOutputBuffer` (closes a connection whose unsent output exceeds the limit; `sendJson` skips destroyed sockets), and applies the 10 KB flood limit, measured in UTF-8 bytes, to a single message instead of the whole receive buffer, which disconnected miners that sent a burst of complete shares in one TCP segment. Adds `maxConnections`, `maxConnectionsPerIp`, `maxProtocolErrors` and `handshakeTimeout` options, stops processing buffered messages after a connection is destroyed, fixes the invalid-share window reset (`this.shares` instead of `_this.shares`, so the ratio was measured over the connection lifetime), truncates the worker label used in logs to 64 characters, only bans an address when `banning.time` is above 0, and unrefs the ban purge timer. |
| `lib/pool.js` | Block submission is retried only while no daemon has answered and at least one failure is retryable (`offline`/`request error`); authentication, HTTP and parse errors are not retried. When no daemon accepted the request the block hex is logged for manual `submitblock`. A block is reported accepted only when `getblock` returns its hash with a numeric `confirmations` above zero (main chain). The daemon reports -1 for side-chain blocks (the coinbase is neither in the active chain nor the mempool), and a missing field is not treated as acceptance. Startup progress reporting tolerates failed RPC results. The init RPC check treats only `null`/`undefined` results as failures, because `getdifficulty` can legitimately return `0`. `SubmitBlock` classifies every `submitblock` response (acknowledged, rejected, not processed, ambiguous) from the pinned daemon's behaviour, keeps that evidence across attempts, looks the block up with `getblock` before each retry and logs the manual-recovery hex whenever every daemon returned an error. `ReconcileBlock` polls `getblock` on all daemons (`blockReconcileAttempts`, `blockReconcileRetryMs`) and sets `shareData.blockStatus` (`accepted`, `side chain`, `unresolved`), `blockStatusReason` and, for a block that is not accepted, `blockHex`; it never reports a block as rejected, and logs when daemons disagree. `SubmitBlock` no longer gives up when any daemon returns an error: it logs each failure, retries while every daemon is unreachable (`blockSubmitAttempts`, `blockSubmitRetryMs`), logs the block hex for manual submission if retries run out, and otherwise lets `getblock` decide whether the block was accepted. Emits `blockSubmitting` (height, hash, worker, block hex) immediately before `submitblock` so the host can persist the block first. Truncates client-supplied text (malformed messages, unknown methods) in logs to 64 characters. Logs rate-limit and output-buffer disconnects. Logs rejected connections (rate-limited), protocol-error and handshake disconnects, and truncates the logged unknown method name. |
| `lib/jobManager.js` | `processShare` rejects non-hexadecimal `extraNonce2`, `ntime` and `nonce` and lower-cases them before the duplicate check, so case variants of an accepted share are duplicates and malformed fields are not hashed as truncated headers. |
| `lib/daemon.js` | Every RPC request now completes exactly once within a wall-clock deadline (10 seconds, overridable per daemon with `timeoutMs`). HTTP 401/403 (`unauthorized`), other non-2xx statuses (`http error`) and empty or malformed bodies (`parse error`) are reported as errors instead of leaving the request pending; socket errors, resets, truncated bodies and timeouts are `request error`, and a refused connection is `offline`. Only `offline` and `request error` are treated as retryable. `isOnline` checked `results.error` (always undefined), so it always reported online; it now checks each result. The `password` property of each daemon instance is non-enumerable so it cannot be serialised into logs. Every request uses its own connection (`agent: false`, `Connection: close`): a request written to a reused keep-alive socket whose peer had vanished stayed in the kernel send queue after the pool's deadline and was delivered once the network returned, so a block the pool had reported as not submitted was accepted later. |

`diff -r vendor/stratum-pool/lib <upstream>/lib` shows every change.
